passage: At Monday's meeting in the Johannesburg office, Lucia showed a slide titled "Route Consolidation Plan" and said, "I've been working on this." Thabo recognised every line. He had emailed her the same numbers last Wednesday. His face grew hot as their manager, Ms Dlamini, nodded approvingly. He did not speak. Afterwards he found Lucia at the kettle. "Lucia, that plan came from the sheet I sent you on the fourteenth. Can we tell Ms Dlamini it was joint work?" Lucia hesitated, then said she had forgotten to mention it. That evening Thabo saved his sent email with its date and wrote Lucia a short recap of who had done which part. From then on he sent his updates to the whole team.

qa.q: What was the title of Lucia's slide?
qa.a: The slide was titled "Route Consolidation Plan."

qa.q: How did Thabo feel when Lucia presented his numbers, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He felt hurt and angry, shown by his face growing hot, yet he stayed silent in the meeting.

qa.q: What did Thabo do that prevents this happening again?
qa.a: He raised it calmly with Lucia in private, kept the dated email, sent a recap of roles, and began sending updates to the whole team.

qa.q: How might Lucia see the conversation at the kettle?
qa.a: Lucia hesitated and said she had forgotten, which may mean she was caught off guard or embarrassed rather than openly defensive. 😅

grounding: A colleague presents Thabo's work as her own; he raises it calmly with evidence and shares updates in writing.

passage:
In the hospital's quality-improvement meeting, Kavitha presented a new idea for shortening the wait at the pharmacy counter: colour-coded tokens for refill patients. The medical superintendent nodded. "Excellent thinking, Kavitha."
Zainab sat very still. She had suggested exactly that in the pantry two weeks earlier, with a sketch on a napkin.
Her first urge was to speak up right there: "That was mine!" She pictured the room turning, Kavitha's face burning. She didn't.
After the meeting she found the email she'd sent Kavitha the next morning, sketch attached, subject line "pharmacy token idea". Then she asked Kavitha for a word in the empty meeting room.
"Kavitha, the token idea is the one I sent you on the 4th. I'd like us to tell the superintendent it came from both of us, and I'd like to be on the pilot."
Kavitha went pink. "I... forgot where it came from. You're right. I'll email him today."
From then on, Zainab put every idea in writing, copied to their supervisor.

qa.a: Colour-coded tokens for refill patients at the pharmacy counter.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling in the meeting?
qa.a: Angry and betrayed; she wanted to shout "That was mine!" but held back.

qa.q: How did Zainab raise the issue calmly?
qa.a: She found her dated email with the sketch, spoke privately to Kavitha, asked for shared credit and a place on the pilot, and afterwards put ideas in writing copied to the supervisor.

qa.q: How did Kavitha respond when Zainab spoke to her?
qa.a: Embarrassed; she went pink, admitted Zainab was right, and agreed to email the superintendent.

grounding: Shows a colleague presenting one's idea as theirs, and raising it calmly with evidence and keeping future ideas in writing instead of a public blowup.

passage:
Hi Arohi,
I wanted to write this rather than bring it up in the team meeting.
In Tuesday's review with the client, the customer-churn analysis was presented as "my analysis" on your slide. Most of the model and the three charts on slides 6 to 8 were my work; our shared folder shows the versions from 12 and 15 May. I was surprised and honestly a bit hurt, and I'd rather talk about it than let it sit.
I'm not asking for anything dramatic. Could you mention to Srinivas that the model was mine when you send the follow-up today? And for the next project, can we agree at the start who owns which part, and put our names on those slides?
I've enjoyed working with you, and I'd like to keep doing it without this being awkward.
Keerthana

qa.a: The three charts on slides 6 to 8, along with most of the model.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel after Tuesday's review?
What makes Keerthana's email a calm, effective response?
qa.a: It cites evidence (the shared-folder versions from 12 and 15 May), makes one small, specific request, and proposes agreeing roles at the start of the next project.

qa.q: How might Arohi feel reading the email?
qa.a: Embarrassed, but given an easy, private way to put it right.

grounding: Illustrates having one's work presented as a colleague's, and raising it calmly with evidence and clarifying roles early for next time.
